messages:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool eu-west-1-pool-3 steady-state CPU 92%, queue latency p99=1.8s, autoscaler headroom 6%. Error rate up ~4% vs baseline. Affected model(s): llama-70b-serving. Dash: https://console.redwood/example/dash/pool/eu-west-1-pool-3

oncall-bot: Paging Maria (oncall week). Escalation policy: eng-platform -> eng-oncall -> eng-sre.

Maria: ack, I'm on it. Pulling up traces and per-tenant QPS. Anyone seeing correlated deploys? :eyes:

Jake: not seeing any deploys. Traffic shows a single tenant spiking ~10x since 2026-03-15T10:12Z: tenant id acme-marketing. Lots of long-running streaming sessions (~12k tokens avg). Could be a bot or bad retry loop.

Maria: ok. Two immediate mitigations on the table: 1) enable burst capacity / increase max replicas on pool, 2) apply temporary quota override to the noisy tenant. Which first?

Liam: we should do both in quick order. Pool has reserved burst nodes (billing tier: dedicated-burst). Current autoscaler: min_replicas=2 max_replicas=20. We can set max_replicas=40 for 30m and flip burst on. Command (unsafe in prod — double-check):

```
# enable burst and raise max replicas
rwctl dedicated update-pool --pool eu-west-1-pool-3 --autoscaler.max_replicas 40 --enable-burst true --burst-duration 30m
```

Maria: I'll run that now and then patch a quota for acme-marketing to 10 RPS and 50 concurrent requests. If it's a runaway client, that should protect others.

Maria: running command now...

infra-bot: Action executed: update-pool eu-west-1-pool-3 by Maria at 2026-03-15T10:18:34Z. autoscaler.max_replicas set to 40, burst enabled, burst-duration 30m.

Jake: good. Next apply tenant quota override via admin API. Suggest limiting tokens-per-minute as well. Example call: 

```
# apply tenant quota override
rwctl tenants update --tenant acme-marketing --quota.rps 10 --quota.concurrent 50 --quota.tokens_per_min 20000 --note "temporary mitigation 2026-03-15"
```

Maria: applied quota override. infra-bot: confirm?

infra-bot: Tenant quota updated for acme-marketing by Maria at 2026-03-15T10:19:12Z. New quotas: rps=10 concurrent=50 tokens_per_min=20000.

customer-signal-bot: Customer reports: several timeouts from small set of users of acme-marketing. Severity: medium. ETA for next status update: 15m.

Liam: also propose a lightweight traffic-shaping rule: route requests from acme-marketing to model-llama-13b for requests < 512 tokens and to llama-70b only if within quota. That buys capacity and reduces GPU usage. Routing rule example: 

```
# add routing rule
rwctl routing add --match "tenant==acme-marketing && input_tokens<512" --target model-llama-13b --priority 100 --duration 60m
```

Jake: can do. Pushed rule at 10:20Z. infra-bot: routing change logged.

infra-bot: Routing rule added by Jake at 2026-03-15T10:20:48Z.

Maria: initial signs look good — overall queue latency dropping to p99=900ms, error rate falling. Burst nodes are online. :thumbsup:

Sophia: taking over follow-up. I'll watch the pool for 30m, ensure autoscaler ramps down after burst window, and open a post-incident doc if the quota hit is repeated. Maria handing off to me at 10:22Z.

Maria: handing off to Sophia. Major talking points: 1) burst enabled + max_replicas=40, 2) tenant quota override applied, 3) routing rule to smaller model for small requests, 4) async-search feature still enabled but we should consider disabling if noise persists.

Sophia: noted. I'll also schedule a temporary feature toggle to limit async-search concurrency for dedicated pools:

```
# feature toggle (platform console / API)
rwctl features set --name async-search --scope pool:eu-west-1-pool-3 --max_concurrent 10 --duration 60m --reason "mitigation acme-marketing surge"
```

Liam: one more thing — cost note: burst nodes are billed at premium; finance notified. Also open an alert to rollback if cost > $X in the window.

Sophia: will monitor costs and set an alert. If traffic doesn't subside after 30m, we'll escalate to account team and consider throttling API keys.

Maria: TL;DR: mitigations applied, customers recovering. Follow-up actions: incident writeup, check acme-marketing client behavior, consider per-tenant burst quotas, and add automated detection for runaway tenants.

Sophia: I'll own the writeup and schedule a postmortem with infra + sales to contact the customer. Monitoring will watch for 1h after rollback window.

Jake: thanks everyone. If anyone sees a secondary spike, ping me directly. :eyes:

Maria: thanks — closing this thread for active triage.

Sophia: marking as handed off. continuing watch. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
